Publication boundary

Copyright and Quotation Policy

The archive publishes original summaries and evidence locators, never reproduced scripts, scans, panels or book excerpts.

Public pages use original expression

Public pages may publish identifying metadata, independently written summaries, factual lore points, relationship maps and official-source links. Transmedia records do not publish dialogue, captions, OCR text, translated excerpts, page-by-page retellings, panels, cover art, scans or downloaded editions.

There is no automatic safe word count or percentage for copying another work. When a source is a book, comic or other expressive work, the archive's default is no verbatim quotation and no visual reproduction unless a separate rights review documents permission or a narrowly necessary exception.

Names, titles and brand use

Titles, character names and short identifying labels are used only to identify the subject of independent commentary. The archive does not imply publisher approval, reproduce publisher branding as its own, or present source material as a substitute for an official edition.

Private research material

Research copies, OCR output and full working transcripts may be used privately for checking names, speakers and claims. They must stay outside the public repository unless their publication has been explicitly approved. The repository guard rejects common raw-text, transcript, scan and ebook fields or file formats from public lore paths.
